145. Rail is the most preferred mode of transport for domestic tourists. Though many tourist
places are covered by railways, amenities in the train as well as at the railway stations have to
be improved substantially for better tourist experience.
146. The Committee recommends that air connectivity to major small tourist places
should be explored keeping in view the increase in number of tourists to make the tourist
places more popular. The Committee also notes that there is need to connect hill stations
by deploying aircrafts and helicopter services for increased connectivity.

27
147. The Committee was informed that both Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Tourism
have agreed to collaborate in the upgradation of 24 railway stations in the country. The
Committee recommends that this plan should be implemented immediately and in the next
year’s railway budget  more railway stations should be included for similar upgradation.
148. The Committee also recollects its experience during the study visit to Darjeeling
wherein the roads, NH-31 and NH-55 right from the Bagdogra airport to Darjeeling is in
dilapidated condition. The Committee is surprised as to how the tourists will be attracted
to such destinations. The Committee recommends that the road stretch may be taken up
for renovation and repair on a priority basis.
149. In addition, at various places in the north-eastern circle  and hilly regions ropeways
and other modes of transport other than the road journey can be considered for connectivity
purposes. The success of  Konkan railway could be replicated with  the possibility of tunnels
and bridges for inter-connecting the different hills.
150. The Committee is also of the view that to develop connectivity in Islands of A& N
and Lakshdweep Islands , intra- island connectivity should also be promoted so that distant
islands can also be visited by tourists.
Inter-Ministerial Coordination
151. Ministry of Tourism informed the Committee that active convergence in the resources of
various sectors involved in promotion of tourism at Central and State level is necessary for
achieving the optimum results. The approach paper to the XII
th Five Year Plan, prepared by the
Planning Commission, stresses the need to develop formal and informal links between all
stakeholders and coordination across all levels of Government. Ministry of Tourism is already trying
hard for ensuring the convergence amongst various stakeholders. For achieving the best results in
Convergence, following are proposed:-
/head2rightA Committee may be constituted under the Chairmanship of Prime Minister with
members from concerned Ministries such as Culture, Civil Aviation, Road Transport &
Highways, Urban Development, etc.
/head2rightA Committee may be constituted in each State/UTs under the Chairmanship of Chief
Ministers/Administrator with members from concerned Ministries of the State
Governments/UT Administrations.
/head2rightPlanning Commission may help the Ministry of Tourism in sorting out the issues with
other Ministries/organisations at Central level as well as with the State.
/head2rightPlanning Commission may increase the Plan outlay of Tourism departments of various
States/UTs while finalizing their Annual Plan outlays every year.
152. Regarding the inter ministerial coordination the Secretary, Tourism during deliberations has
informed that :
“….First is that an Inter-Ministerial Group has been set up with the Home Ministry
representative at the Joint Secretary level, Ministry of External Affairs and our Ministry, that
is, Tourism.  Wherever we are getting specific complaints about visas, these people operate
on the e-mail and through e-mail they are able to, in most of the cases, help them out, if
not totally resolve. I have requested my colleagues to maintain accurate statistics so that
we can actually give the figures as to how many interventions have been successful.”
153. The Committee is of the opinion that tourism development could not be done in
isolation as various Ministries and Departments other than Tourism Ministry have pivotal

28
role in it. The Committee therefore welcomes the step taken to have convergence in the
decision making and execution process with the help of various committees constituted for
the purpose. The Committee also hopes that the above may be a dynamic forum to speedy
implementation of projects solving all the bottlenecks coming in the way.
Tourism Promotion and LTC
154. To promote tourism in NE region and J& K, the Government has extended the facility of
LTC to Government employees. The Committee came to know that with the increase of tourists
in these places the tourism sector has got a boost. There is a need to invest more in the basic
facilities.
155. The Committee likes to recall various representation received from the stake holders as
regards extension of LTC by private airlines to Jammu and Kashmir, which is a live example for
the boom in domestic tourism activities as a result of the Leave travel concessions to the
government employees. However, the Committee noted that Air India is not able to take the
increasing load of passengers particularly in vacations. To remedy the situation, the Air India
may be requested to increase the number of seats offered under ‘Air India Holidays’ within
the limits of LTC-80. It is learnt that relaxation for travel by air to North East States has
been further extended for 2 more years beyond May 2012. The Committee feels that facility
of availing LTC by private airlines for North-Eastern states may be extended to Government
employees. Keeping in view the demands from its stakeholders from Jammu & Kashmir the
Committee further recommends that relaxation for travel by air to Jammu and Kashmir
may be extended beyond June, 2012.
156. Regarding the extension of LTC relaxation to travel by air to people visiting Southern States
the Ministry of Tourism informed that relaxation of Home Town LTC provision has to be issued
by the Ministry of Personnel and Training to encourage domestic tourists in the Southern States.
In this regard, States in the Southern Region have been requested to furnish their comments. The
Ministry informed that a  request has also been sent to the Ministry of Civil Aviation to furnish
their comments in the matter.
157. The Committee recommends that more and more tourist places should be included
in extending this facility to boost tourism in the country.
General Observations and Recommendations
158. The Committee while appreciating the efforts made for tourism development and
‘Incredible India’ campaign recommends that the unexplored paradise should not remain
unexplored. But efforts should be made to provide adequate facilities to develop the
unexplored places to attract more tourists.
159. The Committee appreciates the ‘Clean India’ concept propagated by the Ministry. The
Committee recommends that it should have a major focus from the grass root levels.
Therefore, the local bodies and civic agencies should be made part of the drive and
incentives and financial aids should be extended. The most important thing is strict
monitoring of the success levels accompanied by media campaigning to spread the message
across the length and breadth of the nation.
160. The Committee observed that the MoU with Ministry of Civil Aviation may yield good
results in the coming seasons. Also the cleanliness oriented initiatives at the major railway
stations of the country may be effectively implemented so as to develop them at par with
the airports as far as cleanliness is concerned. The Committee also recommends that ads

29
on the train bogies both inside and outside giving message of the importance of cleanliness
will be able to convey the message effectively among the masses.
161. The Committee notes that the Elephanta caves of Maharashtra are lacking adequate
tourist facilities and other developmental activities. The Committee therefore recommends
that concrete plan for the Elephenta Caves may be formulated at the earliest.
162. The Committee notes that the region in and around Kumarakom and Alleppy in
Kerala are famous for backwaters and houseboats thereby  attracting tourists from India
and abroad.  The bird watching facilities in Kumarakom is also world famous.  However, this
tourist destination need a lot of improvement and development to make it a world class
tourist attraction. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism in
coordination with the Government of Kerala should formulate a master plan for
comprehensive development of the Kumarakom Alleppy region as a major tourist
destination.
163. The Committee also suggests that Ministry of Tourism should take initiatives with
the State Governments’ tourism departments for better delivery of services to the visiting
tourists.

30
OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
Analysis of Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12)
The Committee notes that  the total allocation made for the Eleventh Plan was
Rs. 4997 crore and the Ministry was able to spend Rs. 4690.57 upto Dec., 2011. The
Secretary while deposing before the Committee stated that:
…..Sir, that  we are one of the few Ministries in the Government of India which has  done
nearly 100 per cent. So, Sir, we hope that tourism will now go to a different orbit, if not
a different zone.
(Para 6)
The Committee also notes that as per year-wise utilization detail (Table I) submitted
by the Ministry, the total utilization during the Eleventh Plan had been around 98% on an
average. The Committee appreciates that Ministry of Tourism was able to spend the allocation
during the Eleventh Plan and hope that the tourism sector must have got benefitted by the
funds that have been put into the sector through various schemes. (Para 7)
Product/infrastructure Development for Destinations and Circuits
The Committee is of the opinion that even though the Ministry was able to incur the
surplus expenditure under the scheme, it is equally important is to know reasons for excess
expenditure as the desired targets have not been achieved in terms of creation of
infrastructural facilities  and the resultant tourist arrivals. The Committee also emphasizes
the need for a thorough review of the physical achievements made on the infrastructure
projects of the Ministry during the Eleventh Plan period. (Para 11)
The Committee notes that the work of the “Integrated Development of Buddhist
Circuit at Lalitagiri, Ratnagiri, Udyagiri and Langudi”  in Odisha was sanctioned during the
Tenth Plan period and is still going on. In the past also, the Committee has drawn the
attention of the Ministry of Tourism to a number of projects which were taken up and
crores of rupees were invested therein but could not be completed and later on, were
dropped. This results in wastage of taxpayers money and country’s scarce resources. The
Committee also desire that information regarding the status of projects sanctioned before
the Eleventh plan period which are still continuing may be submitted to the Committee. The
Committee also  recommends that the projects involving large amount of investment should
be monitored carefully during the implementation stage itself  to ensure that work is
completed in time and investment made therein do not go waste. (Para 12)
The Committee recommends that the proposal of the State Government of Madhya
Pradesh for developing Jabalpur as a mega circuit for development of tourist infrastructure
may be taken up by the Ministry of Tourism at the earliest. (Para 13)
Externally Aided Projects
The Committee notes that out of the allocation of Rs. 25.65 crores, the Ministry
could spend only Rs. 20.78 crores. The Committee also notes that the Ajanta-Ellora project
has not yet completed as some major work on the part of ADI, MTDC and MJP are pending.
30

31
It is expected to be completed by July, 2013. The Committee emphasizes the need for proper
monitoring and coordination be ensured with all agencies concerned to complete the project
on time. (Para 16)
Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITM/NIWS
The Committee noted that Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITM etc was Rs.495.00 crores as
per Planning Commission outlays but the actual allocation was Rs. 387.70 crores only but
actual expenditure being Rs. 393.43 crores. Thus, there is over spending. The Committee,
however, is not convinced with the achievement in ratio of the expenditure. There is need
for more focussed approach and opening of more institutes for this purpose. (Para 18)
Capacity Building for Service Providers
The Committee notes the cuts made in the outlay for capacity Building for service
providers scheme wherein the outlay stands at Rs.95.00 crores and the allocations are
Rs.89.00 crores. The actual expenditure of Rs. 67.79 crores shows that total allocations could
not be utilized by the end of the Plan period. This is disappointing mainly because Ministry
of Tourism is underutilizing the fund meant for skill development at a time when India is
faced with huge shortage of trained and skilled people in the tourism and hospitality
industry. We must have functional linkages with need of the industry and academic
institutions specially IHMS, IITM, CCI, NIWS, etc. (Para 20)
Overseas and Domestic Promotion
The Committee notes that  extra allocation of Rs.145 crore was made for the
Overseas Promotion and Publicity including Market Development Assistance as the plan
outlay was only Rs.1010 crores but the total allocations stands at Rs.1155 crores. Compared
to other projects, the expenditure pace is also very prompt in this case as Rs 1024.00 crore
has been incurred upto 31
st Dec. 2011, whereas in the case of Domestic Promotion and
Publicity including Hospitality there was a cut in allocations amounting to Rs.81 crores  as
the allocation of Rs.345 crore was made against an outlay of Rs.426 crore. The expenditure
stands at Rs. 315.85 crore. The Committee notes that the expenditure on Domestic
Promotion has no such momentum in comparison to  the expenditure pattern of the
Overseas promotion. The Ministry has admitted that 3/4
th of the economy in the tourism
sector is contributed by the domestic tourists and domestic tourists has witnessed a growth
of more than 10%. (Para 21)
The Committee, while appreciating efforts to tap tourism market overseas, the
growing domestic market should not get ignored. The Committee feels that there is a need
for being little careful in utilizing funds for this purpose as on overseas promotion an over
expenditure of Rs.145 crores in 2011-12, has been noticed. The Committee would like to
have a clarification in this regard. (Para 22)
Incentives to Accommodation Infrastructure
In the case of Incentives to Accommodation Infrastructure, the Committee noted
that  the total allocations have been considerably reduced, mere Rs.66 crore was allocated
out of Rs.235 crore outlay. The Committee feels that during Eleventh Plan period the
project was not properly implemented by the Ministry as per the expenditure pattern and
this late hour wake up for more allocations could have been avoided. The Government has
identified that there is a shortage of 2,26,040 hotel rooms by 2016. In such a scenario

32
underutilizing the fund meant for creating accommodation infrastructure reflects that there
is something wrong. The Committee, therefore, recommends to revisit this programme
during the Twelfth Plan period so that more funds are allocated in the coming years and
utilized it effectively. (Para 23)
Computerization and Information Technology
The spending pattern on the computerization and Information technology is also very
poor as the total expenditure stands at Rs.57.30 crores out of outlay of Rs 121.00 crores
and allocation of Rs 83.50 crores. In this case also the Committee noticed a reduction of
about 1/3 on the allocations in comparison to the total outlay. The Committee notes that
lack of fund is not a hindrance to technological advancement. What is lacking is the
required will power to implement the programmes and utilize the money effectively. The
Committee recommends that the detailed review may be made to ascertain, in the age of
technological advancement where most of the tourist promotion are dependant on websites
why Ministry of Tourism is unable to tap the potential. (Para 24)
Market Research including 20 Years Perspective Plan
The total spending for Market Research including 20 years Perspective Plan stands
at Rs.14.49 crores, whereas the expenditure is Rs.19.50 crores. The Committee notes that
States like Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, West Bengal, Odisha, J&K and
Rajasthan which are having greater tourism potential were not covered. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the remaining States need to be included in the next phase.
(Para 26)
Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Projects
The total outlay under this head was Rs.200 crores and allocation was of RS. 89.20 crores,
whereas the actual spending has been at Rs.26.57 crores only. The Committee noted that
Assistance to Large Revenue Generating Projects received a lukewarm response from private
investors. The Ministry has submitted that now it has  proposed to include projects such as hotels,
amusement parks, theme parks etc. within the ambit of the scheme. In view of poor response
received for the Assistance to Large Revenue generating Projects as accepted by the
Ministry itself, the Committee recommends that the scheme be reviewed and redesign and
the new guidelines may be framed to attract more entrepreneurs to utilize the scheme.
(Para 27)
Creation of Land bank for Hotels
The Committee notes that creation of Land Bank for Hotels could not pick up during
the Eleventh Plan period as the amount of Rs.12.02 crores actually allocated for the purpose
remained fully unutilized at the end of the Eleventh Plan. The Committee recommends that
this project may be reviewed so that amount, though symbolic, of Rs.1.00 crore for the year
2012-13  earmarked for the purpose is utilized. (Para 29)
Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism infrastructure development
The Committee observes that Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism
Infrastructure Development was provided extra allocations of Rs.7.01 crore over and above
the total outlay of Rs.25 crores, i.e. Rs.32.01 crore whereas the spending stands only at
Rs.20.51 crores. The Committee feels that this is the result of poor planning and

33
implementation of the project. The Committee also recommends that if there is any
bottlenecks at the administrative level for the scheme, it should be properly revisited and
necessary corrective measures need to be taken. (Para 31)
Salient Features of the Twelfth Five Year Plan
The Committee appreciates the optimism reflected in the Ministry’s higher targets
specifically for Foreign Tourist Arrival, Domestic Tourist Arrival, Foreign Exchange earnings
and employment generation from tourism during the Twelfth
 Plan period. The Committee
recommends that Planning Commission may be persuaded not to reduce the allocation so
that the objectives of Twelfth Plan are achieved. (Para 37)
As regards the imparting ‘pro-poor approach’ during Twelfth Plan aimed at increasing
net benefit to the poor from tourism and poverty reduction, the Committee finds it better
said than done. It may be theoretically unquestionable but it is practically difficult to
achieve. We should always aim at something that is in the realm of possibilities and closer
to ground realities. (Para 38)
As for employment figures in tourism given above, the Committee would like to
know what kind of employment and for how long and with what income. We should avoid
making vague claims in respect of employment in tourism sector. The Committee would like
to have full facts about this data with necessary details. (Para 39)
The Committee is not aware of the mode of collection of data on employment in
tourism. Regarding employment whether it is remunerative employment or otherwise is not
known to the Committee. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the method of
collection of data and on employment in tourism sector and the organisations involved in
it may be furnished to the Committee. The Committee may also be intimated about the
details of the sector-wise employment in tourism sector. (Para 40)
Budgetary Allocations for 2012-13
The Committee is concerned to note that against projected amount of Rs.2000 crore,
only an amount of Rs.1210 crore has been approved by the Ministry of Finance/Planning
Commission for 2012-13 that is going to drastically affect various future plans for growth
of tourism proposed by the Ministry of Tourism. Since the tourism inflow is expected to be
doubled by the end of the Twelfth Plan period. Keeping in view various targets fixed by the
Ministry regarding the requirement of additional infrastructure, manpower and other
facilities, tourist flow, etc., the Committee recommends that additional funds may be
earmarked for the Ministry of Tourism so that their future development  plans may be
progressed as proposed. (Para 46)
Product/Infrastructure Development for Destination and Circuits
The Committee notes that RE allocation of Rs.582.99 crore for Product/Infrastructure
Development for Destination and Circuits was made in 2011-12. The allocation was optimally
utilized to Rs.567.23 crore upto February 2012 with the likelihood of remaining allocation
to be utilised by March, 2012. The Committee, however, is of the view that spending the
entire allocation should not be the only criteria of success of the scheme, it should also be
measured in terms of actual infrastructure it has established. (Para 57)
The Committee appreciates that State Level Monitoring Committees (SLMC) have
been set up to regularly review the progress of tourism infrastructure projects. The

34
Committee, however, recommends that SLMCs in all the States should be created and
monitoring done at regular intervals to check the progress of projects. (Para 58)
For identifying tourist circuits and destinations, there is need to make the States
pro-active by giving them assistance in selecting the same in each States so that it is spread
evenly throughout the country. (Para 59)
The Committee notes that the scheme covers a vast array of infrastructure for which
funds could be utilized such as cruise terminal, adventure facilities, waste/sewage
management, signage, etc. The Committee recommends that the scheme needs to be
publicized and effective coordination with various Ministries/Departments initiated and close
monitoring of proposal for development of cruise terminal, luxury trains like palace on
wheels etc. be done regularly. (Para 60)
The Committee notes that religious tourism and pilgrimage are inherent part of
Indian Culture and people are going to pilgrimage for centuries irrespective of the fact that
there exists tourist infrastructure or not. The Committee further notes that if appropriate
tourist infrastructures are developed at all the pilgrim centres, more and more pilgrim
tourists from  India and abroad can be attracted to those places. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that appropriate modern tourist infrastructure may be developed at all the
pilgrim centres of the country. For this purpose Ministry should take concerted steps to
select circuits and destinations to be covered under the scheme of Product/Infrastructure
Development for Destination and Circuits. (Para 61)
The Committee came to know that the Durga Hatkati Temple situated at the Shimla
District of Himachal Pradesh is  famous  and thousands of  pilgrims including foreigners
are visiting the place annually. The tourist facilities are lacking there and beautification
works also need to be done. Ministry of Tourism may consider the development of the
temple in consultation with State Government a priority basis to facilitate tourist pilgrims.
(Para 62)
The Committee is of the view that the development of tourism clusters in rural areas
is a welcome initiative. The Indian traditional arts and crafts are now a days on the verge
of extinction and such a step is required to rejuvenate the traditional artisans and cottage
industry of the country which are now sidelined and finding it difficult to face to
competition  posed by the global products and trends. The Government, however, has to
take concrete action to ensure that the benefits of tourism growth under “pro-poor
approach” should reach to the weaker sections of society, particularly, the craftsmen.
(Para 63)
The Committee is also of the view that markets in the metro cities should also be
developed in collaboration with traders association and should be provided assistance from
the scheme of Product/Infrastructure Development for Destination and Circuits. In this
regard the M.G. Road market at Gangtok can be emulated as it has become a “place must
visit’ not for its market but by being sold “Tourist Spot” as the place has been developed
to attract tourist. (Para 64)
Tourism Promotion and Publicity
The Committee notes there is a regular growth in the domestic as well as foreign
tourists during the Eleventh Plan period except during 2009 because of the global recession
as informed by the Ministry of Tourism. Even though India has vast variety of tourist
attractions from ancient to modern, the global tourism share is less than 0.6% annually in

35
terms of world arrivals. The Committee feels that this percentage is just unacceptable, and
what we are aiming at is to achieve 1% during the Twelfth Plan. (Para 78)
The Committee notes that the expenditure incurred upto February 2012 is Rs.194.26
crore for overseas promotion. The Committee is of the view that the expenditure is not
commensurate with the return in the form of number of Foreign tourist arrivals i.e. 5.78
million in 2010. The Committee is surprised that with so many attractions-religious, tourist,
health etc. why we have not been able to attract enough tourists to India. The Ministry’s
effort should have to be to tap this potential. Here again, the Committee have doubts about
the overseas promotion campaigns. The Committee recommends that the Government must
have re-look into the necessity of various tourism promotion offices abroad and the efficacy
of various officials under Overseas Promotion and Publicity. (Para 79)
The Committee notes that one of the reasons for low tourists arrival could be lack
of cleanliness among others. The Committee further notes that  only Rs.10.00 crore has
been made available under this head for Clean India Campaign. The Committee is of the
view that a substantial part of the allocation under this head may be diverted for ‘Clean
India Campaign’ as the tourist will come only when our tourist places are clean and well
maintained. With focussed approach for cleanliness once our tourist destinations/
infrastructural facilities reaches the world standard more and more tourists will come.
However for this the purpose discussions should be also be held with the state and local
agencies to make it more effective at the grassroot level. (Para 80)
The Committee comments the Government of Goa for the initiative to take up major
clean up operation along Roads and Beaches and hope that it will become a model to be
emulated by States in other tourists destinations. (Para 81)
The Committee also recommends that alongwith aggressive marketing in this age of
technological advancement the our websites should be more attractive and interactive and
secure so that tourist can book from the site itself. This will gradually reduce the
expenditure on marketing and promotion. The Committee also recommends that redressal
mechanism should be made available in the website itself and reply should be given to the
persons concerned which will also help in the form of feedback from the visitors/tourists for
making tourism destinations in India more responsive. (Para 82)
The Committee notes that the number of Indians going abroad for tourism has been
on increase with 17.4% in 2010 thereby indicating that even domestic tourists are not being
attracted.  The Committee is of the view that we should try to further increase domestic
tourists’ movements in the country as well. The Committee therefore recommends that
there should be a review on the spending on the overseas and domestic promotion projects
so as to ensure that domestic promotion projects get due priority in terms of allocation of
funds. (Para 83)
Training
The Committee notes that there are 33 Institutes of Hotel Management and 7 FCIs
which are conducting various courses of National Council for Hotel Management and
Catering Technology for training Manpower. The Committee keeping in view the projected
requirement of 47.26 lakhs employment  in 2012-13  is of the view that the IHMs and FCIs
may not be able to handle the demand.  The estimates provided by the Ministry of Tourism
states that the training capacity at the end of Eleventh Plan stands at 8342 intake for UG/
PG courses, 5546 for Diploma/certificate courses and 36340 for short duration courses. The
gap in requirement and supply in 2012-13 would be 5.70 lakhs and the annual intakes at

36
various levels are far less compared to the actual manpower demand.  The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the new training institutes proposed to be opened in the coming
years should on the actual requirement of manpower in each stream. The Committee also
recommends that the States which have performed well in promotion of tourism should get
priority while selecting the places for opening such institutes. The Committee also
recommends that private sector participation wherever unavoidable, need to be regulated
and controlled suitably if they fail to achieve the requisite standard. (Para 95)
The Committee notes that for training manpower the Ministry of Tourism has huge
task before it. However, it is doubtful that a provision of Rs.110 crore for the IHMs and
Rs.50.00 crore for the training of personnel in the unorganized sector made in the budget
will be sufficient to meet the manpower training facilities as per the projected demand. The
Committee therefore recommends that the Government should take steps to provide
allocation adequate enough to meet the requirement of trained personnel to serve the
increasing tourism potential of the country. (Para 96)
The Committee notes that the grants are being utilized by very few universities. The
Committee recommends that the universities all over the country may be roped in to avail
the grant and it may be given in those areas where the major tourism potential exists and
states which promotes tourism with vast intervention. The Committee also is of the view
that wide publicity should be given to the scheme so that more Universities are sanctioned
the grant. (Para 97)
Accommodation Infrastructure
The Committee notes the step taken by the Ministry to encourage Budget hotels.
The Committee is of the view that to reduce this shortage some incentives have to be given
for construction of new hotel rooms particularly in the Budget Category hotels.  The
Committee is also of the view that concerted efforts need to be taken to meet the massive
requirement of 22,60,040 hotels rooms by 2016. The Committee emphasizes the need for
putting a scientific methods in place to collect the information regarding the actual
availability of hotel accommodation in the country. In this exercise, the State Governments/
UTs as also the local bodies should be involved. (Para 100)
The Committee, also in view of the assessment made by the Ministry on the above
scheme recommends that the Ministry should impress upon the State Governments to offer
new initiatives for the creation of quality accommodation to the visiting tourists. Central
assistance may be extended for achieving this goal and the new criteria may be worked out
for achieving this. (Para 101)
North East Region
The Committee notes that the North-Eastern States are getting adequate funds infact
more than 10% during the last three years. This has helped in creation of infrastructure
and other facilities in the region. However, the Committee feels there remains a lot to be
done in terms of provision of  hotels and connectivity. The facilities are not adequate to
meet the requirements of increased number of tourists. The Committee also notes that with
no five star hotels in the region, it is resulting in loss of revenue as high end tourists are
not turning up. The Committee recommends that it is time to wake up to augment tourist
facilities and for this Ministry of Tourism should review their schemes and seek active
participation from States to get more projects implemented. The Committee also would like
to emphasize that Tourism in North East Region is the main source of livelihood as such
it should be provided all the support from the Ministry of Tourism. (Para 105)

37
The Committee however notes that the response to the capital subsidy scheme has
not been encouraging although potential (of setting up 2 star category hotel) is there. The
Committee in this regard reiterates its recommendations contained in  its 172 nd Report which
is reproduced below:
…The Committee has observed that most of the states are not geared up for the
conventional tourism in respect of accommodation - affordable hotels and guest houses.
They do not have good and affordable accommodation, both  in terms of numbers as well
as quality. This was also evident from field trips to these States. There is no Five Star Hotel
in NER till date. The Committee notes that Government of India has launched the scheme
for capital subsidy of 30% for hotels (not below 2-star category) with effect from 1
st April,
2008 for a period of five years. However, this scheme has not been successful in this region
in achieving the desired results…
(Para 106)
The Committee, therefore, would like the Government to see as to why the funds
for setting up of convention centres are not being utilized. The Committee, also notes that
despite of enough funding in the NE region there is dearth of basic facilities there and even
the projects sanctioned by Ministry of Tourism is not getting good responses. (Para 107)
Tax Structure
In the Working Group Report pertaining to Ministry of Tourism it was stated  that in
majority of the tourist destinations abroad, the luxury tax is ranging from 5 to 7 percent only,
however, it is 4 to 20 percent in various states of India. The Committee observed that affordable
destinations are major tourism attractions for medium and low income tourists. However it is more
important that the tourists facilities also should not be compromised in the effort of making it
affordable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the tax incentives should be as
pragmatic as to generate maximum income. At the same time, there should not be any
compromise on the quality of the services provided. (Para 111)
The Committee observes that the investment linked tax incentive for new hotels of
two star category and above anywhere in India need to be reviewed so that tax incentive
for hotels is available for below 2 star accommodation and the domestic tourism mostly
consisting of middle class are also benefitted. (Para 112)
The Committee observes that the broad scope of economic activities involved in
tourism enables wider participation of people in its growth including the participation of the
informal sector. However, one of the major constraints to the tourism growth is multiplicity
of tax with high rates. The Committee therefore recommends that adequate tax exemptions
may be given to the tourism sector to ensure its growth in all the possible areas of the
country. Therefore, the Committee also recommends that both the Central and State
Governments should work out a uniform tax structure in the tourism sector. (Para 114)
The Committee notes the steps taken for seamless travel which was initiated during
the Commonwealth Games to facilitate tourists by the NCT of Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana
and Uttar Pradesh and recommends that similar exercise should be taken to emulate the
model by other States. (Para 116)
The Committee notes that the above recommendations of the Ministry of Tourism for
rationalised tax structure; introduction of a system of single point payment of taxes and
online transaction system for smooth traffic movement merit due considerations. The

38
Committee therefore recommends that Ministry of Tourism should further pursue the
matter with all the State Governments and Union Territories to avoid multiple tax
structures and provide single window payment of taxes for tourism and tourist operators.
(Para 119)
The Committee was informed that the proposal for allocation of a separate “TV” series
registration for tourist vehicles and one time/annual payment of taxes would facilitate smooth
movement of tourist traffic as it would do away with the requirement to stop for payment of taxes
at State borders. Ministry of Tourism recommended the implementation of a separate “TV” series
registration for tourist vehicles in the long run. The Committee also supports the view of the
Ministry to provide “TV” series registration for tourist vehicles and one time/annual
payment of taxes to be implemented by all the concerned agencies without any delay.
(Para 120)
Environmental Issues and Eco Tourism
The Committee recommends that the Committee constituted for the purpose should
finalize the report in time bound manner and make stringent laws to protect the wildlife
and protected areas. (Para 123)
The Committee also notes that a comprehensive waste management system is lacking in
most of the tourist destinations. This will become a serious problem in the coming years because
of the increase in the number of tourists. The Committee also notes that there is  scarcity of water
in almost all tourist places and specially in Hilly areas. This problem is very acute in places like
North Eastern Region, Coastal Region and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Committee during
its recent visits also got many complaints. The Committee recommends that the Ministry
should take up the matter at various levels with State and Municipalities to remove the
problem of  shortage of water and waste management. Eco-friendly toilets are the new
concept which may be explored. (Para 125)
The pollution caused by the plastic products need to be taken as a serious threat
to the environment and the locals and tourists should be made aware of the hazards it
may cause in the region. The Committee recommends that for tourists, carry-bags from
local handicrafts should be made available with slogans on environment and tourism.
(Para 127)
Isolation of Island Region in Tourism Development
The Committee notes with dismay that the tourism potential in the Islands in India
is, in fact  more than the popular tourist destinations like Thailand, Singapore, Hawai etc.
However, the insufficient facilities have marred the scope of these amazing Islands. So far,
there is no such guide map prepared for benefiting the scenic beauty of these areas as a
major tourist attraction. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a special tourism
focus should be given to the Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands for tourism
promotion. (Para 129)
The Committee is, however, of the view that tourism activities should not be allowed
to be detrimental to the environmental balance. The Committee is of the view that there
should be strict adherence to the environmental regulations while promoting tourism. Our
environmentally fragile areas could not be blindly opened for access to the tourists; however
the regulations should not be applied uniformly in a country like India where the diversity
of geographical distribution is maximum. (Para 130)

39
Cruise Tourism Potential
Ministry of Tourism provides funds to Major Ports for development of cruise tourism.
However, so far only Mormugao Port Trust has submitted project for financial assistance. The
Committee is of the view that the scheme need to be discussed with all the Ports and
appropriate initiative may be taken to implement the cruise tourism projects in all the
Ports. (Para 134)
The Committee was also informed of the high taxation rates for Yatch, boats, ships which
are registered in India. This leads to people preferring to go to other countries. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the tax structure should be rationalized to attract more tourists
from abroad. (Para 135)
The Committee had the occasion to visit cruise terminals at some of the ports. The
Committee noted the absence of basic facilities and poor maintenance of the terminals. The
Committee recommends that to make cruise tourism success in India there is need to make
the terminals more accessible and attractive. (Para 136)
The Committee recommends that the well developed water ways in the states like
Kerala, Goa, Maharashtra, Assam, in the Kolkata- Varanasi route and Kolkata Sunderbans
need to be focused for cruise tourism facilities. The Port Trusts of Goa, Cochin, Mumbai,
Chennai and Mangalore may be financially aided for fulfilling the ‘hub – a home port”
concept. (Para 137)
The Committee notes that in the Western Coast down through Sindhudurg to Goa
have beautiful virgin beaches which are untapped and are equally attractive as overseas
destinations like Singapore to Caribbean and to Mediterranean. The Committee
recommends that a sea route from Mumbai down to Goa  and Mangalore connecting all
these beaches need to be developed which has tremendous tourism potential. (Para 138)
The Committee also recommends that appropriate Rules and Regulations may be
formulated for  regulating  cruise tourism to ensure planned growth of the sector. Further,
there is need to put strict rules for ensuring safety measures such as provision of safety
equipments like life jackets, trained manpower etc. (Para 139)
The Committee during its visit also noted that there is lack of well maintained boats
and small cruises in A & N Islands. The Committee recommends that the boats should be
upgraded to attract more tourists in A & N Islands. (Para 140)
Connectivity and Tourism
The Committee was informed that State roads still have to be developed. The
Committee recommends that suitable mechanism may be developed to get these 13 state
roads completed by utilizing funds from the Central Road Fund (CRF) available with the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in a time bound manner. (Para 142)
The Committee recommends that air connectivity to major small tourist places
should be explored keeping in view the increase in number of tourists to make the tourist
places more popular. The Committee also notes that there is need to connect hill stations
by deploying aircrafts and helicopter services for increased connectivity. (Para 146)
The Committee was informed that both Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Tourism
have agreed to collaborate in the upgradation of 24 railway stations in the country. The
Committee recommends that this plan should be implemented immediately and in the next
year’s railway budget  more railway stations should be included for similar upgradation.
(Para 147)

40
The Committee also recollects its experience during the study visit to Darjeeling
wherein the roads, NH-31 and NH-55 right from the Bagdogra airport to Darjeeling is in
dilapidated condition. The Committee is surprised as to how the tourists will be attracted
to such destinations. The Committee recommends that the road stretch may be taken up
for renovation and repair on a priority basis. (Para 148)
In addition, at various places in the north-eastern circle  and hilly regions ropeways
and other modes of transport other than the road journey can be considered for connectivity
purposes. The success of  Konkan railway could be replicated with  the possibility of tunnels
and bridges for  inter-connecting the different hills. (Para 149)
The Committee is also of the view that to develop connectivity in Islands of A & N
and Lakshdweep Islands, intra-island connectivity should also be promoted so that distant
islands can also be visited by tourists. (Para 150)
Inter-Ministerial Coordination
The Committee is of the opinion that tourism development could not be done in
isolation as various Ministries and Departments other than Tourism Ministry have pivotal
role in it. The Committee therefore welcomes the step taken to have convergence in the
decision making and execution process with the help of various committees constituted for
the purpose. The Committee also hopes that the above may be a dynamic forum to speedy
implementation of projects solving all the bottlenecks coming in the way. (Para 153)
Tourism Promotion and LTC
The Committee likes to recall various representation received from the stake holders as
regards extension of LTC by private airlines to Jammu and Kashmir, which is a live example for
the boom in domestic tourism activities as a result of the Leave travel concessions to the
government employees. However, the Committee noted that Air India is not able to take the
increasing load of passengers particularly in vacations. To remedy the situation, the Air India
may be requested to increase the number of seats offered under ‘Air India Holidays’ within
the limits of LTC-80. It is learnt that relaxation for travel by air to North East States has
been further extended for 2 more years beyond May, 2012. The Committee feels that facility
of availing LTC by private airlines for North-Eastern states may be extended to Government
employees. Keeping in view the demands from its stakeholders from Jammu and Kashmir
the Committee further recommends that relaxation for travel by air to Jammu and Kashmir
may be extended beyond June, 2012. (Para 155)
The Committee recommends that more and more tourist places should be included
in extending this facility to boost tourism in the country. (Para 157)
GENERAL OBSERV ATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
The Committee while appreciating the efforts made for tourism development and
‘Incredible India’ campaign recommends that the unexplored paradise should not remain
unexplored. But efforts should be made to provide adequate facilities to develop the
unexplored places to attract more tourists. (Para 158)
The Committee appreciates the ‘Clean India’ concept propagated by the Ministry. The
Committee recommends that it should have a major focus from the grass root levels.
Therefore, the local bodies and civic agencies should be made part of the drive and
incentives and financial aids should be extended. The most important thing is strict

41
monitoring of the success levels accompanied by media campaigning to spread the message
across the length and breadth of the nation. (Para 159)
The Committee observed that the MoU with Ministry of Civil Aviation may yield good
results in the coming seasons. Also the cleanliness oriented initiatives at the major railway
stations of the country may be effectively implemented so as to develop them at par with
the airports as far as cleanliness is concerned. The Committee also recommends that ads
on the train bogies both inside and outside giving message of the importance of cleanliness
will be able to convey the message effectively among the masses. (Para 160)
The Committee notes that the Elephanta Caves of Maharashtra are lacking adequate
tourist facilities and other developmental activities. The Committee therefore recommends
that concrete plan for the Elephenta Caves may be formulated at the earliest. (Para 161)
The Committee notes that the region in and around Kumarakom and Alleppy in
Kerala are famous for backwaters and houseboats thereby  attracting tourists from India
and abroad. The bird watching facilities in Kumarakom is also world famous.  However, this
tourist destination need a lot of improvement and development to make it a world class
tourist attraction. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism in
coordination with the Government of Kerala should formulate a master plan for
comprehensive development of the Kumarakom Alleppy region as a major tourist
destination. (Para 162)
The Committee also suggests that Ministry of Tourism should take initiatives with
the State Governments’ tourism departments for better delivery of services to the visiting
tourists. (Para 163)

REPORT
Ministry of Shipping was formed in 2009 by bifurcating the erstwhile Ministry of Shipping,
Road Transport and Highways into two independent Ministries. Maritime Transport is a critical
infrastructure for the economic development of a country. It influences the pace, structure and
pattern of development. The Ministry of Shipping encompasses within its fold shipping and port
sectors which also include shipbuilding and ship repair, major ports and inland water transport. The
Ministry has been entrusted with the responsibility to formulate policies and programmes on these
sectors and their implementation.
ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE

assisted by a team of officers in the discharge of his responsibilities.  The following subordinate/
attached offices, autonomous organizations, societies/associations and public sector undertakings
are functioning under the administrative control of the Ministry of Shipping.

PERFORMANCE DURING XI  PLAN
3. During the XI Plan the total outlay was Rs.45,331.00 crore and the expenditure incurred
was Rs.16,746 crores as informed by the Secretary during the course of oral evidence while
scrutinizing the Demands for Grants. For Port Sector, as per Working Group Report (Port sector)
the total outlay was Rs. 30,305.16 crores out of which budgetary support was Rs. 3749.00 crores
and Rs. 26556.16 crores was Internal Extra Budgetary Resources (IEBR).
4. While deposing before the Committee during the course of oral evidence the Secretary
stated:
…..On the Plan side, as you very rightly said, if you look at the outlay and utilization of
the Eleventh Plan, the outlay was Rs. 45,331 crores and the actual expenditure was Rs.
16,746 crores which is 1/3
rd of the total outlay….
…. We have been under-utilising Gross Budgetary Support to the extent of almost 50 per
cent. The plans which our corporations and ports have been making have also not been
materialising. That is why the figure is low. We need to definitely go into the reasons……
5. The Committee was informed that due to various reasons such as delay in various security
related and environmental clearances, delayed approval of new projects, lack of building material
for Tsunami works of ALHW the funds in XI Plan could not be utilized. Besides, problems of
inadequate draft and other facilities at our Ports, old dredgers, high turn round time, which have
slowed the growth of shipping industry.
6. The Committee notes that in the absence of consolidated data for the XI Plan period
with outlay, actual allocation and expenditure for both the Port and Shipping sector, and
there being no physical targets shown, comment on the performance cannot be made.
However, as admitted by Secretary, Ministry of Shipping, underutilizing the Budgetary
support, due to any reason, in Committee’s view, is acceptable only to a limited extent.
7. The Committee was also informed (in the working group report) that only 1/3
rd of the
total outlay of Rs.30305.16 crore during the 11 th plans outlay, i.e. Rs.10388.87 crore was

that the utilization stands at 59.62% (or Rs.7684.61 crore) only. The Committee finds that
this under-utilization was mainly due to reasons such as delay in clearances, approvals, etc.
These are, no doubt, time-taking exercises but if taken up with proper procedure and
formalities as prescribed, it could be expedited easily and quickly. In view of urgent need
to modernize and expand our port facilities and stiff competition with Private Ports staring
at them, we cannot afford to delay projects at our Ports. The Committee recommends that
thorough home work needs to be done before approaching each plan year projects for
optimum utilization of scarce fund allocation.

42. The Committee was informed that the dredger fleet owned by DCI is ageing and need
replacements. Of the 10 TSHDS, seven of them are more than 20 years old and the oldest is 37
years age as of now. Of the 3 CSDs, two of them are 35 and 34 years old. While the dredgers
of age less than 10 years had performed nearly 300 days in an year, those with age more than
20 had worked only for 230 to 260 days. Faced with this situation the following plans had been
made by DCI in order to augment its capacity.
(i) Order had been placed for procurement of 3 nos. TSHD of 5500 cm hopper capacity
at an estimated cost of Rs.1570.22 crores. The expected 226 delivery of these

(ii) 2 nos. TSHD of 9000 cubic million capacity each at total estimated cost of Rs.1300
crores.

CSDS.

tax (PAT) of the DCI for 2010-11 is Rs.523 crores and Rs.40 crores respectively against the
previous figures of Rs.694 crores and Rs.70 crores respectively. The fall in turnover is mainly due
to break down of the dredgers which are old and ageing, clearing the backlog capital dredging
works in Paradip & Goa project and non-deployment of chartered dredgers due to stoppage of
work at Sethusamudram on Hon’ble Supreme Court Orders. The fall in PAT is because of the fall
in operating income. DCI has recently placed order for three dredgers which are expected to join
fleet between Sept, 2012 and Oct, 2014. As such, the capacity of DCI will be enhanced from
2012-13 which will help in increase of turnover. The turnover for 2011-12 is expected to be the
same as than in 2010-11.
46. On a further query of exodus of executives from DCI which has been one of the reasons
for its under performance, the Ministry has given the following reply:
In the post liberalization era, particularly after 2003-04, a number of private dredging
companies have come up. Till then, DCI being the main Indian Dredging Company had the
human resources strength who had the domain knowledge of the dredging in various Indian
Ports. The Private Companies in order to establish themselves had lured some of the
employees of DCI particularly floating employees by offering them better pay packages.
DCI being a PSU does not have much flexibility in the aspects of pay. As such, DCI is
facing shortage in terms of manpower which the Company is trying to over come by
implementing a streamlined career growth policy for the employees, better working
conditions and inducting deck officers passed out of Indian Maritime University etc. The
exodus of manpower is one of the causes for the fall in performance of the Company. While
the main cause being the shortage of capacity due to the ageing of dredgers which is being
overcome by placing of order for three dredgers.

87. The Committee was informed that SCI’s vessel acquisition programme for the Eleventh Five
Year Plan (2007-12) had envisaged acquisition of 62 vessels, entailing an investment of Rs.13,135 crore.
SCI’s acquisition programme progressed smoothly during the first year of the Eleventh plan (2007-08),
with SCI placing orders for 16 vessels. However, during the period 2008-09 and 2009-10, global
financial meltdown affected credit availability and resultant liquidity in the market. The depressed
freight market led to anticipation of softening of asset values, both new building and second hand
and accordingly, most of the ship acquisition proposals were deferred by SCI. SCI placed orders
for only 9 vessels during these two years. Thereafter, a slight recovery was witnessed in the
shipping markets during 2010-11 and SCI placed orders for 11 vessels during the year.
88. Due to the slower pace of acquisitions during the two years 2008-09 & 2009-10,
acquisition of 26 vessels was proposed during the last year of the Eleventh Plan i.e. 2011-12, to
meet the overall Eleventh Plan target of acquisition of 62 vessels. Accordingly, at the BE stage,
outlay requirement for 2011-12 was estimated at Rs. 3712 crore. However, in 2011, with further

18
deepening of the European crisis, markets once again reversed their upward trend and it was felt
prudent to go slow on acquisitions on account of the prevailing uncertainties. Hence, the outlay for
2011-12 was reduced to Rs.2850 crore at the RE stage.
89. With more than 3 years of continuous subdued activity in the shipping market, almost all
shipping companies across the globe have been severely hit. SCI Management has observed that
SCI’s revenue generation has been adversely affected and further acquisitions may lead to depletion
of its reserves. Hence, SCI has not planned any new acquisition during the year 2012-13.
Accordingly, the outlay requirement for 2012-13 of Rs. 2128.49 crores is based on the payment
obligations for vessels already on order and likely investments in Joint Ventures. The SCI
Management will be reviewing the situation on a quarterly basis to streamline its vessel acquisition
plan. However, at the moment, no new acquisitions are planned in the year 2012-13.

104. The Union Budget 2012-13 is beneficial for the Ports and Shipping Sector. The Ports have
been allowed to raise Rs. 5000 crores through tax free infrastructure Bonds. The countervailing

GENERAL OBSERV ATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
115. The Committee is worried about the track record of the Ministry in utilizing the
allocations in the previous years. It is a matter of concern that the underutilization of
allocation in rampant in the Ministry of Shipping. This shows the casual approach to the
implementation of projects. The Committee notes that the end result of such delays will be
cost overruns as well as revenue losses to the organizations.
116. The Committee also recommends that the increased vessel traffic should be utilized
for generating more revenue from the shipping sector. Accordingly, the possibility of
introducing entry/exit toll for the foreign flagged vessels etc. should be worked out by the
Ministry. Also the coastal surveillance need to be strengthened to avoid the accidents and
other such unfortunate mishaps similar to some incidents reported recently.
117. The Committee is of the view that even though the Indian tonnage is growing as per
the projections, the India fleet are not gaining the momentum. Even the fleet acquisition
plans of the SCI has been passing through a very difficult phase. At the same time Indian
ship building industry and ship repair sector are equally struggling to get enough business.
This is happening at a time when Ship Building Orders are given to foreign shipyard and
Indian ships and dredgers are looking overseas destinations for the repair works. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should make an assessment of the
reasons for this contradictory situation and should make remedies for the same.
118. The Committee is concerned over the environmental impact of the ship breaking
activities and the frequent dumping of abandoned vessels and waste materials into the
Indian territorial waters. The Committee recommends for adequate steps to curb the
malpractices in the ship breaking business. The Government should also ensure that old and
unused vessels are not dumped in the Indian Waters.
119. The Committee also notes that Major Ports are getting a raw deal from Government
in many ways. They have to take clearances from both Central and States Governments. In
case of Minor Ports, environmental clearances are taken only from concerned States. The
Committee was also informed that Kandla Port is facing delay in providing road connectivity
for a small stretch of about eight kilometers. This has put Kandla Port in disadvantageous
position vis-à-vis the neighbouring private Minor Port in developing their business. The
Committee is of the view that the interests of Major Ports are not made to languish at the
cost of Private Ports, wherein tax payers crore of Rupees have been invested. The
Committee feels that the Major Ports are loosing business to the Minor Ports; if we
compare the growth rates of the two. The Committee strongly recommends to look into
these aspects and making level playing field for both the Major and Minor Ports.
120. The Committee came to know that in JNPT Port a scanner was setup to scan the
containers a few years back. However the same is not working now. On being asked about
the status of non-functioning of the scanner, the Committee was informed that the entire
management operation and installation of scanner is under the Customs Department and
the Customs Department will install the scanner and operate it. The Committee is of the
view that JNPT and Ministry of Shipping should take immediate action to make the scanner
operational in consultation with the Customs Department. The reasons for the non-
operationlisation of the scanner, till now, may please be furnished to the Committee.
121. The Committee notes that the inland water transport is not being regulated properly
and there are no Rules/Guidelines and if there exists some, it seems it is not being
implemented. The Committee notes one of the worst boat tragedies in Assam, in which
hundreds of people died when a packed steamer carrying over 300 passengers sank in the

23
Brahmaputra river after being caught in a severe storm midstream on 30 th April 2012. The
boat was overloaded, with passengers on its roof. The Committee notes that, it seems, there
is no mechanism in place to check the implementation of safety measures for inland
waterways transport. The Committee recommends that strict enforcement of the Rules
should be ensured by the Ministry to check the recurrence of such accidents.

The Committee notes that maximum number of its barges of DCI are very old. The
Committee hopes that with addition of new barges into the fleet and upgradation of the
existing ones, the DCI may be able to meet the requirement of the Ports.  The Committee
recommends that addition of barges may be done on a fast track keeping in view the
additional dredging requirements of 625.36 Million Cubic Meters as projected for the major
ports and minor ports in the country during the 12
th Plan period. (Para 48)
The Committee also notes that trained manpower is one of the main source of
support of any organization. If executives from DCI will be leaving in such a large number
how the company will perform its work entrusted to it. The Committee recommends that
the Ministry should take corrective measures to stop the exodus. (Para 49)
ANDAMAN AND LAKSHADWEEP HARBOUR WORKS (ALHW)
The Committee notes the fund allocations and utilization during the the 11
th Plan for
ALHW with a total Plan outlay of Rs. 541.82 crores and out of that Rs. 425.58 crores is
the expected expenditure upto 31.3.2012. The Committee notes that ALHW has managed to
spend 78.5% of the Plan Outlay. However, more prompt action is required to ensure that
full amount is expended and the projects are completed well in time. (Para 55)

27
The Committee has noted the statement of the Ministry that the Plan schemes
proposed under the Andaman & Nicobar Islands have been completed by the plan period
itself. However, the Committee found it contradictory to their claim as four major schemes
i.e. replenishing damaged breakwater and approach in Little Andaman, construction of
additional jetty for mainland vessels at Kamorta, reconstruction of office building complex
of ALHW at Port Blair and  development of Jungly Ghat Harbour  are expected to spill
over to the 12
th Plan period. The Committee also notes under utilization of funds during
2011-12 due to various reasons submitted by the Ministry. The Committee recommends that
special stress need to be given to the projects proposed for this isolated area of the country
and should be monitored/reviewed periodically so that development takes place in the A&N
Islands. (Para 56)
DG LIGHTHOUSES AND LIGHTSHIPS
The Committee notes that there has been the optimum utilization of funds during
XI Five Year Plan which is expected to be Rs.198.68 crore against the total outlay of Rs.150
crore. The achievement in targets have been found some positive trend as compared to
other sectors of the entire Ministry of Shipping. The Committee hope that enhanced
allocation of Rs. 90.00 crore in BE 2012-13 will be utilised by making early efforts for
getting necessary clearances at various levels for the projects. (Para 62)
The Committee observed even Light Houses have a history and some of them being
very old and located at beautiful places can be opened to the tourists.  The Committee also
feels the need of more active Light Houses in view of the recent spurt in the vessel traffic
along the Indian coasts. The Committee therefore, recommends that more funds as required
for completion of the above projects, may be allocated. (Para 64)
INLAND WATERWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA (IWAI)
The Committee noted IWAI’s efforts to execute  the projects proposed during 2012-
13 out of the allocation of Rs 130.02 crore and hopes that all the plans would be carried
out in a time bound manner. The Committee recommends that periodic monitoring of the
physical achievements vis-a-vis the financial sanctions need to be made throughout the plan
period. (Para 73)
The Committee notes that water transport has various advantages compared to road
transport. Water transport is cheap, can handle huge volumes of cargo and less impact on
environment. The Committee is of the view that a strong inland water transport system is
able to handle effective, cheap and environment friendly cargo transport mechanism. The
Committee, therefore strongly recommends that the available resources should be
strengthened in order to have a well connected water transport facility through out the
country. (Para 75)
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION LIMITED (CIWTC)
The Committee notes the various steps taken by Government in regard to CIWTC.
The Committee is of the opinion that main reason for non-performance of CIWTC is lack
of working capital and infusion of funds for modernization of construction/production
techniques and no recruitment of manpower and lack of new technology. (Para 83)
The Committee also notes the submission of the Secretary regarding the merger of
CIWTC with IWAI. The Committee has expressed its concern over the future of persons
working in CIWTC. The Committee hopes that the staff of CIWTC will not be forced to

28
opt VRS against individual’s will and CIWTC will be merged with IWAI if the assets of
CIWTC is taken over by it. The Committee also recommends that till the merger process
is completed adequate funds and manpower be made available to CIWTC to carry out its
operations. The Committee also recommends the Government to allow the use of interest
income by CIWTC, which otherwise have to pay income tax on interest income.
(Para 84)
SHIPPING CORPORATION OF INDIA (SCI)
The Committee notes that IEBR has gone down from Rs.2850.00 crore in RE 2011-
12 to Rs.2128.49 crore in BE 2012-13 which shows a declining trend. The Committee is
constrained to note that the SCI has lapsed a majority of funds as against Rs.13,100 crore
in the entire Eleventh Five Year Plan as they have  utilized a little over Rs.7500 crore only.
The Committee views any kind of underutilization of funds seriously. (Para 93)
The Committee is concerned about the financial status of the SCI especially
connected with the ship acquisition programme. The Committee notes that the ship
acquisition programme during 11
th Plan could not materialize due to various reasons and it
has even affected adversely its revenue generation and SCI is in fear of depletion of
reserves. The Committee is also surprised to see the “nil” new proposal during 2012-13
eventhough the targeted acquisition of the vessels are incomplete. The Committee also
agrees with the findings of CAG’s Audit which stated that SCI did not pursue an ambitious
acquisition policy to augment and modernize its fleet and recommends that immediate
corrective measures may be taken by SCI. (Para 94)
The Committee strongly recommends that adequate review on the past policy and
schemes should be worked out and necessary corrective measures should be taken to ensure
the financial health of SCI. (Para 95)
The Committee recommends that SCI should take coordinated action with the PSUs
to ensure that the business opportunities emanating from the PSUs are not siphoned away
by foreign companies. SCI should be in a position to meet the requirements of PSUs by
providing adequate vessels. The Committee is of the view that the SCI is not able to make
use of the favourable situation in enhancing its business volume and a sincere efforts on
these lines are required. (Para 97)
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
R&D is the backbone of any industry to sustain and establish itself. R&D in shipping
sector is the need of the hour as India is one of the major economic powers in the world.
The Committee notes that the Ministry is not utilizing the funds allocated for R&D as only
Rs 0.60 crore could be utilized out of the allocation of Rs.1.58 crore during 2011-12. The
Committee feels that delay in R&D activities might be affected in the long run as one of
the reason for non utilization of funds is lack of technical personnel in the R&D projects.
The Committee recommends that fast track search process need to be initiated for deputing
qualified persons. (Para 103)
TAX PROPOSALS
The Committee feels that the tax benefits and other incentives in the shipping and
port sector will be able to make some relief to the SCI and DCI in their ship and dredger
acquisition projects. (Para 105)

29
PUBLIC-PRIVATE-PARTNERSHIP
The Committee is of the view that PPP model should not be treated as panacea to
give boost to develop all kinds of infrastructure. Role of the Government cannot be
minimized in this regard. The Committee feels that PPP model would be attractive only in
the highly profitable areas, not in non-profitable areas. As such, in Inland Waterways, no
developer is coming forward and no progress is taking place. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that there is need to look into the PPP mode in developing Inland Waterways.
(Para 110)
PROJECT/SCHEME OF NORTH – EAST REGION AND SIKKIM
The Committee notes that in view of the limited scope of work, the entire outlay of
Rs.78.00 crore could not be utilized in 2011-12 for the NW-2 (Dhubri to Sadiya) 891 kms
which only falls under NE region. The Committee wonder when there is no scope to utilize
this allocation why allocation has again been made in Annual Plan 2012-13. The Committee
is of the view that Planning Commission/Ministry of Finance should adopt a realistic view
in the matter to ensure that mandatory allocations for NER from the outlay of Ministry of
Shipping should not remain unutilized. If possible, the above grants be utilized for growth
of Tourism in the region. (Para 114)
GENERAL OBSERV ATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
The Committee is worried about the track record of the Ministry in utilizing the
allocations in the previous years. It is a matter of concern that the underutilization of
allocation in rampant in the Ministry of Shipping. This shows the casual approach to the
implementation of projects. The Committee notes that the end result of such delays will be
cost overruns as well as revenue losses to the organizations. (Para 115)
The Committee also recommends that the increased vessel traffic should be utilized
for generating more revenue from the shipping sector. Accordingly, the possibility of
introducing entry/exit toll for the foreign flagged vessels etc should be worked out by the
Ministry. Also the coastal surveillance need to be strengthened to avoid the accidents and
other such unfortunate mishaps similar to some incidents reported recently. (Para 116)
The Committee is of the view that eventhough the Indian tonnage is growing as per
the projections, the India fleet are not gaining the momentum. Even the fleet acquisition
plans of the SCI has been passing through a very difficult phase. At the same time Indian
ship building industry and ship repair sector are equally struggling to get enough business.
This is happening at a time when Ship Building Orders are given to foreign shipyard and
Indian ships and dredgers are looking overseas destinations for the repair works. The
Committee recommends that, the Ministry of Shipping should make an assessment of the
reasons for this contradictory situation and should make remedies for the same.
(Para 117)
The Committee is concerned over the environmental impact of the ship breaking
activities and the frequent dumping of abandoned vessels and waste materials into the
Indian territorial waters. The Committee recommends for adequate steps to curb the
malpractices in the ship breaking business. The Government should also ensure that old and
unused vessels are not dumped in the Indian Waters. (Para 118)
The Committee also notes that Major Ports are getting a raw deal from
Government in many ways. They have to take clearances from both Central and State
Governments. In case of Minor Ports, environmental clearances are taken only from

30
concerned States. The Committee was also informed that Kandla Port is facing delay in
providing road connectivity for a small stretch of about eight kilometers. This has put
Kandla Port in disadvantageous position vis-à-vis  the neighbouring private Minor Port in
developing their business. The Committee is of the view that the interests of Major Ports
are not made to languish at the cost of Private Ports, wherein tax payers crore of Rupees
have been invested. The Committee feels that the Major Ports are loosing business to the
Minor Ports; if we compare the growth rates of the two. The Committee strongly
recommends to look into these aspects and making level playing field for both the Major
and Minor Ports. (Para 119)
The Committee came to know that in JNPT Port a scanner was setup to scan the
containers a few years back. However the same is not working now. On being asked about
the status of non-functioning of the scanner, the Committee was informed that the entire
management operation and installation of scanner is under the Customs Department and
the Customs Department will install the scanner and operate it. The Committee is of the
view that JNPT and Ministry of Shipping should take immediate action to make the scanner
operational in consultation with the Customs Department. The reasons for the non-
operationlisation of the scanner, till now, may please be furnished to the Committee.
(Para 120)
The Committee notes that the inland water transport is not being regulated properly
and there are no Rules/Guidelines and if there exists some, it seems it is not being
implemented. The Committee notes one of the worst boat tragedies in Assam, in which
hundreds of people died when a packed steamer carrying over 300 passengers sank in the
Brahmaputra river after being caught in a severe storm midstream on 30
th April 2012. The
boat was overloaded, with passengers on its roof. The Committee notes that, it seems, there
is no mechanism in place to check the implementation of safety measures for inland
waterways transport. The Committee recommends that strict enforcement of the Rules
should be ensured by the Ministry to check the recurrence of such accidents. (Para 121)

Tourism and Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Seventy Eighth Report on Demands for Grants 2012-13 of the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

3. The Committee wishes to express its thanks to the officers of Ministry of Road Transport
and Highways for placing before the Committee the material and information desired in connection
with the subject and for clarifying the points raised by the Members.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 3

1
REPORT
Roads are considered as the lifeline of the country. They play a vital role in the economic
growth of the country in many ways than one. India has a vast road network of 41,09,000
kilometers of which the National Highways and the State Highways together account for 2,29,952
kms. The length of National Highways network is only 76,674 kms. (at present) constituting about
1.9%
 of the total road network in the country and carrying about 40% of the total traffic across
the length and breadth of the country. The number of vehicles has been growing at a rapid pace
of 10 percent per annum. The share of roads in total traffic has been growing from 13.8% of
freight traffic and 15.4% of the passenger traffic in 1950-51 to a projected 62.9% of freight traffic
and 90.2% of passenger traffic by the end of the 2009-10.
2. To cope with this increase, appropriate expansion & improvement of the road network is
necessary. All this requires a massive infusion of funds. Historically, investments in roads,
especially highways, were mainly made by the Government because of the large volume of
resources required, long gestation period of projects, uncertain returns and various associated
externalities. But in recent times, the private sector has been actively involved in the development
and maintenance of the National Highways.
3. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has formulated policy guidelines to
encourage private sector participation in the highway sector, besides providing several incentives
such as tax exemptions and duty free import of road building equipment and machinery. Model
Concession Agreements have also been finalized for major road projects.
4. The Ministry primarily follows the agency system to develop and maintain the National
Highways. Besides the State Governments and the Border Roads Organization, National Highways
Authority of India, an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Road Transport and
Highways, act as agencies of the Central Government. The Ministry has undertaken the National
Highways Development Project which is being implemented in phases and envisages the
improvement of about 54478 kms. of arterial routes of National Highways network to international
standards. The prime focus on developing roads of international standards is on creating facilities
for uninterrupted flow of traffic with enhanced safety features including better riding surface,
better road geometry, better traffic management and noticeable signage, divided carriageways,
service roads, grade separators, over bridges and underpasses, bypasses and wayside amenities.
5. The Government of India is responsible for the National Highways and has three agencies
through which NH works are executed. The Three agencies and their respective areas of operations
are:
(a) National Highways Authority of India (NHAI):- It is an autonomous organization of the
Ministry entrusted with the development and maintenance of certain select stretches of
National Highways. Some of the important programmes being the National Highway
Development Programme including the Golden Quadrilateral and East West & North
South corridors.
(b) State PWDs:- The bulk of National Highways other than the National Highways under
the NHDP are looked after by State PWDs.
(c) Border Roads Organization (BRO):- Looks after many stretches/National Highways in
the North – Eastern Region and Strategic areas.
6. The Ministry is also implementing part of the Special Accelerated Programme for North-
Eastern Region (SARDP-NE) through the Border Roads Organization.
