REPORT
1. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Seventy fourth Report on
Demands for Grants 2012-13 of the Ministry of Civil Aviation which was presented to both the
Houses of Parliament on 27
th April, 2012.
2. Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on the 1 st October, 2012 in
respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report.
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the concerned Ministries. The recommendations of
the Committee contained in the One Hundred and Seventy fourth Report, action taken thereon by
the Ministry and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has
been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
5.  The Committee notes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation was able to spend Rs.40.673.04
crores (anticipated) as against the allocation of Rs.49,267 crores for the Eleventh Plan period
resulting in a huge saving. The Committee finds that except Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi
which spent Rs.41.00 crore against the budgetary allocation of Rs.42.00 crore for the plan period,
all other organizations under the Ministry could not spend the allocated money fully. This is a
disturbing scenario. The Committee notes that Air India was able to spend Rs.25,603 crores only
against the allocation of Rs.32,730.71 for the Eleventh plan period, again saving a sum of Rs.7,127
crores. The Committee is surprised to note that when the national carrier was knocking the doors
of financial institutions to bail it out, it was unable to spend money it had been allocated during
the Eleventh Plan period.
(Recommendation at para 6 of 174
th Report)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6. The Eleventh Plan approved outlay of Rs.32730.71 crores of Air India Limited did not
include any budgetary support from the Government. The entire outlay was proposed to be met
from the internal and extra budgetary resources of the company. The actual outlay during this
period 2007-08 to 2011-12 was Rs.24,763.36 crores including equity infusion of Rs.3200.00 crores
by the Government of India. The reduction in the actual expenditure as compared to the Eleventh
Plan Outlay is primarily due to delay in delivery of B787 aircraft due to production related issues.
Further there was a reduction in the other capital projects due to the liquidity crisis faced by the
company during this period as only operationally essential projects were undertaken.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
7. Another case of under-spending is that of Airports Authority of India, the leading
infrastructure provider for aviation industry in the country. AAI could spend Rs.11,873.41 crores
against the allocation of Rs.12,964.21 crores for the plan period. The Committee is not able to

2
understand the logic behind Airports Authority of India’s inability to spend even the budgetary
support of the Government; they could spend roughly 50% only. The Committee feels that such
under utilization of funds by AAI could have definitely slowed the pace and process of developing
airport infrastructure at various places including Chennai and Kolkata. A curious case in this respect
is that of the Hotel Corporation of India which was able to spend Rs.43.75 crores against Rs.75.00
crores. The Committee feels that time has come to assess the performance of this PSU in a
broader perspective and it should not be allowed to become a liability to pave the way for its
privatization. Air India Charters Limited is another example in this respect. They could spend only
Rs.2088.16 crores against the plan outlay of Rs.2475.26. Neither the Low Cost Carrier of the
Government is expanding its services nor able to spend the allocated plan outlay. The Committee
would like to be informed about the reasons for such under-utilization of funds by various
organizations of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and the remedial measures taken to prevent such
happenings in future. The Committee hopes that the Ministry will ensure that the organizations
under its control were able to spend their allocations to the maximum possible extent in the Twelfth
Plan. The Committee feels that any laxity on spending of allocation will have the direct impact on
aviation sector of the country.
 (Para 7 ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
8. AAI incurred an amount of Rs. 11868.41 crores as capital expenditure for development of
airport Infrastructure in the country during Eleventh Plan as against plan outlay of Rs.12964.21
crores which is 92% of plan outlay. The shortfall of 8% has been mainly on account of non-
availability of site, delays in obtaining necessary regulatory and statutory approval, environmental
clearance, and approval from Planning Commission etc. During the period 2007-08 to 2009-10, AAI
spent the entire amount approved in BE by MoCA in respect of schemes for which Government
Budgetary Support (GBS) was provided. However during the year 2010-11 and 2011-12, AAI was
able to spend only 50% of the funds allotted for GBS Schemes mainly on account of delay in
approval from the Planning Commission for various new projects i.e. Jalgaon, Gondia, Puducherry,
Itanagar, Cheitu (Kohima), Jammu airport schemes. The pace of work at mega projects namely
Kolkata and Chennai did not slow down due to non-availability of funds as the funding of these
projects was met out of the internal resources of AAI and borrowings. The delays occurred due
to other reasons.
9. The total outlay in the eleventh plan for Hotel Corporation of India (HCI) was Rs.75 crores
to be spent out of the Company’s own internal resources. However, due to the lower internal
generation during the Eleventh Plan period, HCI was able to spend only Rs 43.75 crores. At no
stage has the Company received any grants from the Government in the Eleventh Plan. The
approved outlay for Eleventh Plan for AICL was Rs. 2475.25 crores. The actual outlay for the plan
period was Rs. 2070.27 crores. The main reasons for reduction in actual expenditure as compared
to the Plan outlay were as follows:
(a) The plan outlay for aircraft induction was estimated based on certain aircraft prices
at certain exchange rate. The actual delivery price was slightly lower on account of
concessions/discounts obtained from Boeing on Aircraft list price compared to our
estimates and exchange fluctuation.
(b) It was assumed that five spare engines would be acquired in the plan period. As
against this, only four spare engines were acquired.
(c) The budgetary outlay was proposed based on estimates of internal revenue generation
which did not materialize. No Government budgetary support was given to AICL
separately.

3
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
10. The Committee notes the reasons furnished by the Ministry of Civil Aviation for
under-utilization of funds by Air India and Airports Authority of India during the Eleventh
Plan period. The Committee notes that most of the outlays that Airports Authority of India
and Hotel Corporation of India could not spent were to be arranged out of internal
resources. However, Public Sector Undertaking which set up out of tax payers’ money can
not be absolved over the lack of commitment merely because no Government budgetary
support was given to them. The Committee hopes that the Ministry will impress all the
organizations under its purview to spend the allocated funds during the Twelfth Plan to the
maximum extent.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
11. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation was not able to spend fund allocated
in respect of DGCA, BCAS and AAI – three main organizations. It is not a welcome sign since
allocation under these heads constituted major share of the allocation under Plan, excluding Air
India. The reasons submitted by the Ministry for under-utilization of funds such as delay in
clearances to various projects, delay in acquisition of land for airport projects and delays in getting
necessary regulatory and statutory approvals may be understandable but not acceptable, if repeated
every year, For example, the project of construction of office buildings for DGCA and BCAS could
not be taken up for last two to three years. The Committee feels that failure to spend the allocated
moneys by these organizations shows a lack of proper planning for timely execution of major
programmes/projects. Delay on account of various administrative problems and procedural
difficulties cannot be acceptable as excuse as these could be visualized at initial stages and
precautions taken well in time. The Committee recommends that the long pending construction of
headquarters for DGCA and BCAS be started at the earliest in coordination with agencies concerned
and be completed in a fixed schedule. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should
impress upon all the organizations under its purview to spend the allocations cent percent in a
planned manner.
(Para 9 ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
12. Construction of DGCA and BCAS Headquarters building is held up because the land at
Safdarjung Airport has been declared as “recreational green” by Ministry of Urban Development.
Secretary, MoCA, Chairman, AAI and DGCA, all have made collective efforts to get the title of
Safdarjung Airport changed in Delhi Master Plan but have not succeeded. Hence the construction
of above offices could not commence for the proposed buildings, though environmental clearance
has been obtained, drawings finalized and approved. AAI is ready to take up the construction and
the day the title for Safdarjung Airport is restored as Airport, the actual construction work will
commence.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
13. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
14. The Committee after scrutinizing the allocations for 2012-13 finds that apart from equity
infusion to the tune of Rs.4000 crore for Air India under the budgetary support, the allocation for
the Ministry is inadequate. The allocation of Rs.738.80 crores under the Non-plan for the year

4
2012-13 is lesser than the allocation at Revised Estimates of Rs.764.86 crores for the year 2011-12.
The Committee expresses its concern over the static allocation to the Ministry which concerns with
one of the fastest growing sectors having lot of potential for further growth. The Committee hopes
that the Ministry will take up its case with Planning Commission for allocations of adequate funds
at RE stage so that ongoing aviation projects are not hampered and new ones are taken up.
(Para 14 i bid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
15. The observation of the Committee has been noted for compliance and its recommendation
will be conveyed to the Department of Expenditure/Planning Commission for seeking enhanced
budgetary allocations at RE stage. Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation has already written to the
Planning Commission seeking higher allocation in the Twelvth Five Year Plan.
Air India
16. The approved outlay Annual Plan 2012-13 for Air India is Rs. 4928 crores, of which
Rs.4000 crores is the budgetary support in the form of equity infusion. Financial Restructuring Plan
and Turnaround Plan of Air India has been approved by the GOI in April, 2012. As per the Plan,
the total amount receivable as equity from GOI in 2012-13 would be as under:
1. Upfront Equity Rs. 5,550 crores
(Rs. 6,750 crores – Rs. 1,200 crores)
provided in the Budget 2011-12 and already received
2. Equity for guaranteed loans
FY 2011-12 Rs. 1,786 crores
FY 2012-13 Rs. 1,787 crores
3. Equity for cash deficit (FT 2012-13) Rs. 1,539 crores
4. Equity for NCD’s Rs. 352 crores
T
OTAL Rs. 11,014 crores
17. Of the above, Rs. 4000 crores has already been provided in the Plan budget of 2012-13.
Ministry of Finance shall be approached to provide for remaining amount of Rs.7,014 crores as
Supplementary Grant in 2012-13.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
18. The Committee feels that Air India is still in critical phase. Any laxity in any matter
relating to Air India can play havoc to the public sector carrier. The Committee notes the
reply of the Ministry. The Ministry, therefore, should pursue with Planning Commission
vigorously for allocation of requisite funds at RE stage so that the ongoing Air India
projects are not delayed.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
19. The Committee notes that the national carrier had to undergo a tough period during the last
year mainly on account of merger related issues, ever increasing ATF prices, employees’ resentment
over non-payment of dues, allotment of profitable routes to private carriers, its over-ambitious
aircraft acquisition plan, inability to raise funds from the open market and the reluctance of
financial institutions’ and Oil Marketing Companies to help the ailing Air India. The Committee finds

5
that though the company was able to increase its passenger load factor it witnessed a dip in share
in domestic and international aviation markets.
(Para 30 ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
20. Air India, the national carrier of India, has proposed to induct capacity in an effort to re-
capture the market share in the domestic and international market. To achieve this, various
measures are being taken as per the Turnaround Plan approved by the Government.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
21. The Committee notes that a large number of amendments to Air Service Agreements with
foreign countries were signed for expansion of international air services by the national carrier
during the last year. The Committee finds that Air India operates almost 500 departures daily
offering more than 78000 seats per day connecting about 150 domestic city-pairs and 125
international city pairs with a 143 strong fleet but still not in a position to attain a visible
competitive edge vis-àvis other airlines. The Committee notes some serious efforts being made both
by Air India management and the Government for taking the national carrier out of the current
mess. There are improvements on some parameters indicating that things have started moving into
required direction, which is why the Government has decided to support the airlines’ recovery
process. But in view of the several challenges and over all slow down in the Sector, Committee
would like to caution the Air India management and the Government to be very careful while
implementing its restructuring/revival plans. The greatest challenge it must overcome on priority is
that relating to HR issues created due to ill-conceived merger plan. The Committee hopes that
allocation of unutilized bilateral /traffic rights to Air India will benefit it in regaining its lost market
share in international market.
(Para 31 ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
22. Air India is given first preference while allocating the traffic rights for international sector.
Air India has submitted their proposed operation plan upto winter 2013. Grant of traffic rights for
other airlines is considered only after taking into consideration the operational requirements of Air
India. Most of the amendments to ASAs done in recent years has not been done for the expansion
of Air India’s services. In view of its losses, Air India has been conservative and has 
not asked
for more traffic rights. It may be mentioned that rapidly increasing capacity, as recommended,
could escalate the losses. The aim should be to increase profitability and competitiveness by service
quality, reliability and revenue generation. Once a profitable model is established, the capacity could
be scaled up rapidly to increase profits further.
23. As regards attaining visible competitive edge vis-à-vis other airlines, following actions have
been taken by AI with respect to network and schedules:
(a) The aircraft on AI’s fleet are mostly new and standardized in term of in-flight comforts
and facilities.
(b) All the major domestic and international routes are operated with the newly acquired
aircraft.
(c) The timings of international services have been rationalized. AI now offers convenient
late evening/midnight hour departures with arrival in morning hours at destinations on
most of the international routes. Further uniform timings are also offered on all days
on almost all international routes.

6
(d) Multiple daily services with uniform timings are offered on all major domestic routes
providing convenient same day return facility.
(e) Conveniently scheduled non-stop services have been introduced on India-N America
routes which is perceived as a Unique Selling Proposition (USP).
(f) The network of AI and its subsidiaries now spreads over to 64 domestic (covering all
remote areas of country) and 33 international destinations (covering North America,
Europe, Far east, South-East Asia, South Asia and Middle East) connecting 159
domestic city-pairs and 127 international city pairs on 305 domestic departures and 175
international departures daily.
(g) Delhi hub operationalized with 2 arrival/departure banks for long haul services. AI now
connects Delhi with 23 international and 48 domestic destinations. AI handles 2800
transfer passengers every day at the Delhi hub comprised by feeder traffic from/to
interior points in India and destinations in neighboring countries mainly Bangkok and
Kathmandu at this stage.
(h) With the merger and integration of the networks of erstwhile AI and IC, operation of
Hub and Spoke services have been increased to provide for convenient connections at
DEL/BOM for passengers originating at other metro cities including Ahmedabad, Goa
and Amritsar. The passengers traveling by the Hub and spoke services avail of
customs/immigration facilities at their point of origin/destination.
(i) Further, services carrying through flights numbers to onward international destinations
are operated from select interior points in India so as to improve AI’s ability to more
effectively market these destinations at the interior points.
Improved website
24. For enhancing customer satisfaction and for improving sales through website, effective
September, 2011, new webmaster and core team was designated with the objective of making the
website as customer friendly and making it as a marketing tool to enhance direct sales thereby
reducing distribution costs and other costs related to bookings through other channels i.e. agents,
portals, booking offices etc.
Initiatives taken so far
• The travel/ticketing rules and regulations related to customers are being updated on real
time basis (which has become an ongoing process now) to enhance customer
satisfaction.
• Constant development and modification of Website and Web page contents as per
market and commercial requirement (which has become an ongoing process) which in
turn enhances customer satisfaction.
• To make it comprehensive platform and single window for all e-business activities and
major source of revenue for AI.
• To enhance the speed and processing time the website has been migrated to NIC
platform (Government of India) effective January, 2012 which in turn enhances
customer satisfaction.
• The refund processing time has been reduced to couple of days to restore customer
confidence.

7
• The helpdesk response time (to respond to customer queries) has been reduced to
24 hours by augmenting the entire set-up to tune it to market requirement.
• A short term web based scheme has been launched effective January, 2012 to
encourage customers for web based bookings/ticketing.
• Aggressively using website as e-marketing tool for advertising promotional schemes,
destinations, new flights, schedule, fares etc.
25. These initiatives have helped Air India to restore confidence of e-customers, change the
focus of website i.e. customer related and above all increase direct sales i.e. web sales. At present
the percentage of web sales is approximately 10% of the total passenger sales on network basis
now. In order to enhance the direct sales (web sales) further, some of the major initiatives under
process or in the near future are:
• To make our site truly global and globally accessible site with regional foreign
languages option.
• To make it interactive and user friendly.
• To make it as major channel of revenue generation, competitive and at par with other
booking portals.
• Use as an effective platform to reduce unsold inventory levels.
• In the long run to develop website as interactive tool for
o Customers
o Prospective business clients
o global networking
o Press releases/information tool about our products, features etc.
o Blog writing, linking and development
o Platform to patronise and bring people closer, who matter for our business on
global basis
o As international tool for marketing, sales, publicity and promotion etc.
o Platform for developing business, partnerships and associations
o Platform for co-promotional, co-branding activities, launches etc.
o Developing data base for promotional activities.
• To link website to other social media networking sites for getting increased traffic with
objective of enhancing sales, constructive publicity and brand building.
• To develop website as tool for electronic media publicity for AI to reduce costs.
• To develop ancillary revenues for Air India by extending options like travel insurance,
visa processing, in-bound tourism etc for its customers.
26. The constant improvisation and modification of website enhances customer satisfaction and
enables the airline to increase its revenues i.e. direct web sales and at the same time reduces
distribution and ticket/booking related costs.

8
Advertising
27. In 2009-10 it was felt that due to the severe cash crunch being faced by the company,
expenditure towards publicity and sales promotion should be kept to the bare minimum. However,
in the current year 2011-12, the company has embarked upon major advertising campaigns in the
various media channels like Television, Print, Radio and Hoardings. Air India has also been
advertising in its website and online channels and just completed an Advertisement campaign on the
recent schemes and product upgrades in all the media channels. Another campaign in the beginning
of February 2012. Air India has also tied up with major events as part of sales promotion. It may
be noted that in contrast to Rs.460.80 lacs spent on Advertising and Sales Promotion during period
April – December, 2010, a sum of Rs.860.70 lacs has been spent on Advertising and Sales
Promotion, during April – December, 2011.
Schemes to promote executive class...
28. AI offers a number of schemes for promotion of Executive Class product on the domestic
network. These include:
– ‘Get Up Front’ Offer:  Air India has launched  an airport upgrade scheme, where
passengers at select domestic airports can pay a prefixed amount of Rs.4000 (distance
up to 750 km.)/Rs.6000 (distance above 750 km.) and upgrade their domestic travel
to Business class, subject to availability of seats and on First Come First Served Basis
at the airport. This scheme is available from 16 Airports in India.
– Upgrade through Option Town: In partnership with Option Town, this is a scheme
to solicit Business class upgrade through Email/SMS. A passenger registers at the
Option Town website and pays the upgrade amount.
– Super Saver Offers:  Air India offers special edition Super Saver ticket booklets with
variants of 4 coupons/8 coupons, which are issued in both Economy and Business
class. These are very competitively priced tickets that offer immense convenience as
each coupon can be used for any city pair on a direct flight,with a few restrictions
within India, as also each coupon can be used by a different person (multiple user
facility).

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
78. In the past year, Air India Express has had to curtail operations due to an acute shortage
of cockpit crew. The problem was aggravated with the implementation of new Civil Aviation
Requirement (CAR) guidelines by the DGCA in February 2012. The new CAR stipulates that rest
hours for the pilots be increased. Further, the number of landings permitted for a pilot at night time
have been restricted from 3 to 2. Pilots are also restricted from operating on two consecutive night
flights. Most importantly, their duty hours have been severely curtailed when they fly in the
“Window of Circadian Low” which has been determined to be between 0200 hours to 0600 hours.
There are further restrictions on their travel as passengers, weekly and daily rest hours etc. These
restrictions have further dwindled the availability of cockpit crew for flying duty. The restricted
capacity is the primary reason for the drop in market share. As the crew situation improves, more
and more flights will be reinstated and new flights introduced. This will definitely provide a boost
to the revenues and market share of the airline. Increased domestic operations are also under active
consideration. Despite the crew constraints, effective April 2012, Air India Express has increased
the Mumbai-Mangalore-Mumbai service from twice weekly to daily. Similar expansion is being
considered for other domestic sectors depending on cockpit crew availability.

107. Regarding increase of service tax, the Minister of Civil Aviation had written to Finance

tickets for Economy class passengers has gone up. However, for First and Executive class
passengers, the service tax element in the ticket has come down from 10.3% to 4.94%.

Island and Lakshadweep) at least 10% of the capacity it deploys on routes in category-I routes,

INTRODUCTION 
  
 I, the Chairman, Department- related Parliamentary  Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture, having authorized by the Commi ttee to present on its behalf, do hereby 
present this One Hundred Eighty Sixth Report on Act ion Taken by the Government on the 
recommendations/observations of the Committee conta ined in its One Hundred Seventy Fifth 
Report on the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Culture (2012-13).  
2.  One Hundred Seventy Fifth Report of the Department-  related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was pre sented to the Parliament on the 7 th  May, 2012 in 
Parliament.  
3.  The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its One 
Hundred Seventy Fifth Report were received from the Ministry of Culture, on 16 
th  October, 2012. 
4.  The Committee considered and adopted the Report as its meeting held on the 5 th  November, 
2012. 
 
 
 
SITARAM YECHURY 
NEW DELHI;                                            Chairman,  
November 5,,  2012                                            Department -related Parliamentary Standing  
Kartika 14,  1934 (Saka)                     Committee on  Transport,  Tourism and Culture.

REPORT 
1.  The Report of the Committee deals with the Acti on Taken by the Government on the 
observations/recommendations as contained in its On e-Hundred and Seventy-fifth Report on 
Demands for Grants 2012-13 of the Ministry of Cultu re which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 7 th May, 2012. 
2.  Action Taken Replies have been received from th e Government on the 16 th  October,  2012 
in respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have been 
categorized as follows: 
3.  The Committee desires that final replies in respect  of those 
recommendations/observations which have been catego rized as interim replies by the 
Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.  
4.  On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Co mmittee has made observations on each 
item of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the co ncerned Ministries. The recommendations 
of the Committee contained in the One Hundred and F ifty-fourth Report, action taken thereon 
by the Ministry and recommendations/observations of  the Committee on each item of action 
taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
5. The Committee notes that out of Rs.3524.11 crore  earmarked for XIth Five Year Plan, 
an amount of Rs.3047.91 crore was spent leaving a s aving of Rs. 476.20 crores.  The 
Committee notes that the unspent amount was mainly in respect of the archives, museums, 
libraries and activities for NE region.  The Committee was informed that due to non-finalization 
of upgradation and modernization programmes and def erment of activities of Victoria 
Memorial and Salarjung Museums, funds could not be utilised under 'Museums '. Similarly, 
Asiatic Society, Kolkata also could not utilize the  grant for modernization of infrastructural 
facilities. The Committee views any kind of under-u tilization of allocations as a lapse, 
especially those due to avoidable reasons.  In this  case, most of the reasons given by the 
Ministry were avoidable ones.   
6. For example, the Committee has seen itself how t he affairs of the National Museum, 
Delhi were being (mis) managed. The Committee in it s 167 
th  Report has conveyed its 
impression about all these aspects and the Action T aken Notes furnished by the Ministry amply 
reflect that even the Committee’s recommendations do not evoke required response/ action. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that being concern ed with art and culture, the Ministry has 
to be pro-active and utilize the allocations judici ously provided for XII Plan. The Committee 
also recommends the Ministry to ensure that the sch emes/ plans do not suffer on account of 
under-utilization of funds and shortcomings/ flaws are corrected during the XII Plan Period. 
(Recommendation at para 9 & 10 of 175th  Report) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
7. In the Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12) an amou nt of Rs.3047.91 crore was actually 
spent against the total allocation of Rs.3524.11 cr ore.  In the XII Five Year Plan (2012-17) the 
Ministry will make concerted efforts to utilize the  Plan funds to the maximum extent through 
regular monitoring in accordance with the recommend ations of the Committee and Finance 
Ministry’s guidelines. 
 

 - 9 - 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF THE COMMITTEE  
8. The Committee is of the view that with the utili zation of overall allocation in the 
Eleventh Five Year Plan,  there is a need to monito r the expenditure in all the heads 
thereby utilizing the allocation judiciously and ca rrying out the activities which were 
actually planned. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
9. The Committee notes with concern that out of Rs. 805.00 crore provided at RE 2011-12, 
expenditure up to 29 
th  February, 2012 was Rs.570.72 crore. The Committee has a doubt if the 
Ministry of Culture would have been able to utilize  the remaining amount of Rs.234.28 crore in 
just one month i.e. March, 2012. If it is so, the s ame is against the established financial norms 
for spending. The Committee deplores the habit of i ncurring expenditure at the fag end of the 
year. The Committee recommends that proper monitori ng of the scheme / plans should be done 
with reviewing of progress in every quarter to ensu re that rushing for last minute expenditure at 
the end of the financial year is avoided. The main reasons for non-utilization and non – 
finalization of upgratation/ modernization plans of  Museums, and non-finalizations of schemes 
which were started in XI Plan period. The Committee  notes that the expenditure is less in those 
areas which are critical for preservation and propagation of Culture and invariably require more 
funds such as ASI, Museums and Archives. The Commit tee recommends that proper planning 
should be made at the time of proposal of the plan/  schemes and an effective monitoring 
mechanism be put in place and ensure that the expenditure is incurred fully and uniformly. 
      (Para 12 i bid  ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
10. As against the BE of Rs.785.00 crore in 2011-12 , which was increased to Rs.805.00 
crore at RE 2011-12, the Plan expenditure was Rs.74 9.00 crore during the financial year 2011-
12, which is about 95.41% of BE and 93.04% of RE 2011-12.  The progress of 
implementation of schemes as well as expenditure un der each scheme is constantly monitored 
at the highest level i.e. Secretary (Culture) and A S & FA (Culture) and meetings are held 
regularly in this regard. Instructions are also iss ued to all Attached/ Subordinate Offices, 
Autonomous organizations and to Divisional Heads in  the Ministry at the beginning of the 
financial year to phase out the expenditure in such  a manner that the quantum of expenditure 
incurred under these organizations/ schemes is sust ained in an even manner over the financial 
year. The instructions of the Ministry of Finance r egarding phasing of expenditure on quarterly 
basis are closely followed and monitored at the highest level. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
11. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that mo nitoring of expenditure will be 
reviewed regularly.  Further, the Ministry should e ndeavor that the utilization of funds 
will be as high as it was during 2010-11. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
12. The Committee was informed that the Ministry of  Culture had projected a requirement 
of Rs.18353.94 crore for the XII Plan to carry out its ongoing as well as new schemes and 
activities. The Committee, however, notes with conc ern that for the year 2012-13, 30% less has 
been given than what was proposed by Ministry of Cu lture. The Committee is of the view that 
the Culture Sector has not received the priority it  deserved. It strongly recommends giving it 
adequate funds for the XII Plan. Ministry’s financi al performance was not bad except in 

 - 10 - 
Museum, Libraries, Archives etc., during the entire  XI Plan period. The Committee hopes that 
the Planning Commission would consider the importan ce of culture and art in human 
development and contribution of culture related act ivities and services to GDP, employment 
generation and above all, instilling a sense of nat ional pride/ identity. The Committee 
emphasizes the need for developing proper linkages not only with the Tourism which is 
conspicuous by absence today, but also with the Min istries such as Road and Highways, 
Transport, Civil Aviation, Railways etc., with a vi ew to having an integrated developmental 
activities for promoting and showcasing our rich cultural and art traditions to the world.  
      (Para 17 i bid  ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
13. Secretary (Culture) had written to Member, Plan ning Commission for favourably 
considering the Ministry’s proposal for an enhanced  allocation for the culture sector during the 
12 
th  Plan period.     
14. An Inter-Ministerial Coordination Committee on Tourism Sector (IMCCTS) has been 
constituted under the Chairmanship of Principal Sec retary to the Prime Minister to sort out 
Inter-Ministerial issues relating to development of  tourism sector in the country. It was, inter 
alia, desired that Ministry of Culture should adopt  a pro-active tourism policy which should 
promote Museums, cultural and heritage sites, besid es monuments as well as to have close 
inter-face with the Ministry of Tourism. 
15. Ministry of Culture and Tourism are accordingly  closely coordinating to address 
tourism related issues. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
16. The Committee hopes that Ministry of Culture wo uld constantly review the 
policies/programs with various Ministries for touri sm related issues.  The Committee also 
hopes that the Ministry of Culture would take the b enefit of schemes of other Ministries 
like Tourism,  for road connectivity to connect important tourist destinations. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
17. The Committee notes that against the projected demand of Rs.2916.43 crore, the 
Ministry of Culture has been allocated only Rs.864.crore for 2012-13, less than 1/3 of what was 
proposed by the Ministry. The Ministry had made plans for utilizing the enhanced allocation for 
schemes like preservation and conservation of monum ents by ASI, introduction of new 
schemes for libraries, celebrating centenaries, str engthening and expansion of ongoing plan 
schemes implemented by Zonal Cultural Centres for c reative industries, benefit of Tribal/ Rural 
artists at grass root level, ten new schemes by Nat ional Archives, financial assistance for 
Professional Groups and Individuals, for Specified Performing Arts, National Mission for 
Monuments and Antiquities, Sangeet Natak Akademi, N ational School of Drama etc., The 
Committee notes the apathy of the Government toward s the cause of preservation and 
promotion of our ancient culture and has allocated plan outlay of less than 1/3 of what was 
proposed by the Ministry of Culture. During the XI Plan also, Art and Culture got a share of 
only 0.16% of the total Central Plan allocation of the Government of India. The Committee 
recommends that Ministry of Culture certainly deserves a better treatment in allocation of funds 
in view of its importance. The Committee recommends  that Ministry should strive to utilize the 
allocations optimally by September by every year so  that while submitting proposal for RE, 
Ministry can justify its stand for more allocation which is based on trend of last 6 months’ 
expenditure. However, the Ministry should also take  extra care/ measures to monitor the 
schemes/ plans on regular basis. 
      (Para 20 i bid  ) 

 - 11 - 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
18. The Ministry is making all possible efforts to optimally utilize its allocation by 
September every year through constant monitoring of  progress of schemes and expenditure 
related thereto. In 2012-13, the expenditure upto the 30 
th  September, 2012, has been 51.98 % of 
the B.E. of Rs.1447 crore, which is as per the instructions of Ministry of Finance. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
19. The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
20. In view of effecting a cut of about 70% in Mini stry’s projected demand, the Committee 
feels that either the Ministry’s projections were u nrealistically high or the Planning 
Commission and Ministry of Finance did not accord t he importance this Ministry deserves. 
There is a need to sensitize the concerned agencies  to appreciate the contribution of art and 
culture to our nation’s life. Ministry has proposed  some very good schemes that were overdue 
and must be taken up on priority. 
      (Para 21 i bid  ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
21. It may be mentioned that while formulating Annu al Plan 2012-13 and XII Plan, 
proposals were invited from all the Cultural Organizations and Divisional Heads of the Ministry 
and on the receipt of proposed outlays, Annual Plan  proposals for the Ministry as a whole were 
prepared, which showed a substantial increase over the approved outlay for the year 2011-12. 
On evaluation and analysis of those proposals, projections appeared to be unrealistic in so far as 
spending capacity of the Cultural Institutions/ Schemes taken into during the XI Five Year Plan. 
These proposals were reviewed and pruned suitably b efore sending them to the Planning 
Commission. A projected demand of Rs.2916.43 crore for the Annual Plan 2012-13 was made 
to the Planning Commission for their consideration,  against which only Rs. 864 crore for 2012-
13, constituting about 30% of the projected demand, has been allocated for the Ministry. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
22. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of C ulture should take up the need 
for more allocations with the Planning Commission a nd Ministry of Finance.  The 
Committee hopes that Planning Commission/Ministry o f Finance would adopt pragmatic 
approach while considering the requirement of funds by Ministry of Culture. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
23. The Committee notes that ASI could incur expend iture of Rs.133.90 crore upto 29 
th  
February, 2012 out of the revised allocation of Rs. 161.75 crore.  The Committee hope that with 
the mandate of its various work, ASI would be able to utilize the resources allocated to it in RE 
2012-13.  The Committee notes the constraints faced  by ASI due to its specific nature of work 
whereby maintenance and conservation is limited to only a few months and also the fact that the 
RE allocation is received in March and as per speci fic instruction of Department of 
Expenditure, the expenditure cannot be more than 33 % in the last quarter and 15% in the last 
month.  The Committee recommends that ASI should ut ilize the allocation in a time frame and 
opt for relaxation on case-to-case basis.  
      (Para 30 i bid  ) 

 - 12 - 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
24. ASI had utilized funds to the extent of Rs.173. 91 Crore up to 31 
st  March, 2012 out of
